coverage: Reviewed the bound example lines 53–68 and its explicit geometric proof, including the cited positive half-twist and stacking conventions.

findings.evidence: Statement lines 55–59 and proof lines 95–98: at n=2, h=1/12 and Q=(-h,h). In η(t)=(-h,-h+2h exp(2πit)), the first coordinate is fixed and the second circles counterclockwise once around -h; their difference is 2h exp(2πit), never zero. Both coordinates return to Q. The bound |−h+2h exp(2πit)|≤3h=1/4<1 keeps the moving point in the open disk. Hence the lifted geometric braid is pure and its endpoint permutation is id.

Proof lines 99–105: the proof constructs an isotopy from σ₁⋆σ₁ to β_round(t)=(-h exp(2πit), h exp(2πit)), then an isotopy from β_round to the displayed η. The round representative has both points rotating once counterclockwise about their midpoint. That is a valid picture of the same braid class, but it is not the literal coordinate motion η, whose first point is stationary. A diagram can show the round model with an isotopy/equivalence cue or explicitly label both representatives.

findings.check: Word order, crossing sign, and endpoint permutation
findings.evidence: Definition source def-elementary-geometric-half-twist and example lines 65, 81, 99–105: positive σ₁ is the anticlockwise half twist: label 1 passes below the midpoint and label 2 above in the fixed horizontal projection. Stacking γ⋆β runs β first below γ, and the induced class product is [γ][β]=[γ⋆β]. The proof stacks two copies, so the word is [σ₁]^2 (two positive half twists/crossings); each σ₁ exchanges the endpoints and the square has identity endpoint permutation. Since the letters agree, the square's written order is unambiguous.

Facts lines 75–87 and proof lines 97–98, 105–107: the orbit map p₂ sends the ordered loop η to an unordered configuration loop, whose unique lift from Q is η; tracing that lift gives βη with class [σ₁]^2. The pure-group identification points the other way: Ψ:G₂^pure→PB₂ sends [βη] to (ι^F_*[η])^{-1}. A diagram of the canonical identification must retain this inverse and its direction; it should not label Ψ as the loop-to-braid tracing map.

findings.check: Local rendered tiles and diagram merit
findings.evidence: All three listed PNGs were viewed at original resolution. They show the example and proof without a diagram; the displayed formulas and proof are legible. The receipt reports zero KaTeX errors, zero TikZ diagrams, and zero diagram failures. A small two-point motion diagram with labels, positive orientation, endpoints, and the isotopy distinction would clarify this concrete example, but absence of art is an editorial opportunity rather than a mathematical or rendering defect.

recommendation: An optional two-strand diagram is useful if it distinguishes the literal η motion from its isotopic midpoint-rotation representative, labels the two positive half twists, and keeps the loop-to-trace direction separate from the inverse pure-group map. The missing-diagram status remains uncertain/editorial.
